added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(\mathbf P=(P_n)\in
\mathcal B_{\epsilon,M,c_0,v_0,v_1}\), the explicit cross-fitted saturated-cell
one-step estimator in \(def:saturated\text{-}one\text{-}step\) satisfies
\[
 \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)
 =\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{P_n}(O_i)
   +o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2}),
\]
\[
 \frac{\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}}{V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)}
 \longrightarrow1
 \quad\text{in }Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\text{-probability},
 \qquad
 \frac{\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)\}}
      {\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)}}
 \Rightarrow N(0,1).
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathbf P=(P_n)\in
\mathcal B_{\epsilon,M,c_0,v_0,v_1}\), and suppress the row subscript on
\(p_k,\pi_k,\mu_{ak}\).  All constants below may depend on
\(\epsilon,c_0,K_0\), but not on \(n,d_n\), or the chosen member of the
triangular class.  By \(def:balanced\text{-}local\text{-}class\), the row
law satisfies \(ass:iid\text{-}sampling\), \(ass:fixed\text{-}overlap\),
\(ass:cell\text{-}mean\text{-}envelope\),
\(ass:conditional\text{-}fourth\text{-}moment\),
\(ass:balanced\text{-}cell\text{-}masses\),
\(ass:local\text{-}dimension\), and
\(ass:efficient\text{-}variance\text{-}band\).  In particular,
all probability-order notation below is under \(Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\), and
\[
 v_0M^2\le V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)\le v_1M^2.
\tag{1}
\]

First derive the nuisance rates.  For a validation fold \(I_s\), let
\(m_s=n-|I_s|\) be its training size.  Since \(K_0\) is fixed and fold sizes
differ by at most one, \(m_s\ge c_Kn\) for a constant \(c_K>0\) and all
sufficiently large \(n\).  Let \(N_{ak,-s}\) and \(N_{k,-s}\) be the
corresponding training arm-cell and cell counts.  Cauchy--Schwarz and
\(ass:conditional\text{-}fourth\text{-}moment\) give
\[
 E_{P_n}[(Y-\mu_{ak})^2\mid X=k,A=a]
 \le
 \{E_{P_n}[(Y-\mu_{ak})^4\mid X=k,A=a]\}^{1/2}
 \le M^2.
\tag{2}
\]
If \(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(m,q)\), integration of its probability
generating function yields
\[
 E[(N+1)^{-1}]=\int_0^1(1-q+qt)^m\,dt
 =\frac{1-(1-q)^{m+1}}{(m+1)q},
 \qquad
 N^{-1}\mathbf1\{N>0\}\le2(N+1)^{-1}.
\tag{3}
\]
Conditionally on \(N_{ak,-s}=r>0\), the fitted cell mean is the average of
\(r\) observations from the conditional arm-cell law, so (2) bounds its
conditional mean-squared error by \(M^2/r\).  When \(r=0\), the zero fallback
in \(def:saturated\text{-}one\text{-}step\) has squared error at most \(M^2\)
by \(ass:cell\text{-}mean\text{-}envelope\).  With
\(q_{ak}=P_n(X=k,A=a)\ge\epsilon p_k\), equations (2)--(3), the lower mass
bound \(p_k\ge c_0/d_n\), and \(\sum_kp_k=1\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E\!\left[\sum_{k=1}^{d_n}p_k
  (\widehat\mu_{ak}^{(-s)}-\mu_{ak})^2\right]
 &\le M^2\sum_{k=1}^{d_n}p_k
 \left\{e^{-m_sq_{ak}}+\frac{2}{(m_s+1)q_{ak}}\right\}\\
 &\le C_{\epsilon,c_0}M^2
 \left\{e^{-c_{\epsilon,c_0}m_s/d_n}+\frac{d_n}{m_s}\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
For the propensity estimate, condition on \(N_{k,-s}\).  On a nonempty cell
the empirical treatment proportion has conditional variance at most
\(1/(4N_{k,-s})\); on an empty cell its squared error is at most one.
Projection on \([\epsilon/2,1-\epsilon/2]\) cannot increase distance from
\(\pi_k\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\).  Repeating (3) gives
\[
 E\!\left[\sum_{k=1}^{d_n}p_k
  (\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}-\pi_k)^2\right]
 \le C_{c_0}\left\{e^{-c_{c_0}m_s/d_n}+\frac{d_n}{m_s}\right\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Assumption \(ass:local\text{-}dimension\) implies
\(n/d_n\gg\sqrt n\), so the exponential terms in (4)--(5) are negligible
relative to \(d_n/n\).  Markov's inequality applied to (4)--(5), for each of
the fixed number of folds, yields
\[
 \|\widehat\mu_a^{(-s)}-\mu_a\|_{P_n,2}
   =O_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(M\sqrt{d_n/n}),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat\pi^{(-s)}-\pi\|_{P_n,2}
   =O_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(\sqrt{d_n/n}).
\tag{6}
\]

Define the uncentered augmented score
\[
 g(O;\eta)=m_1(X)-m_0(X)
 +\frac{A\{Y-m_1(X)\}}{e(X)}
 -\frac{(1-A)\{Y-m_0(X)\}}{1-e(X)},
\tag{7}
\]
where \(\eta=(e,m_0,m_1)\), and let
\(\eta_0=(\pi,\mu_0,\mu_1)\).  Conditional-mean definitions,
\(ass:fixed\text{-}overlap\), and \(def:ate\text{-}functional\) give
\[
 E_{P_n}[g(O;\eta_0)]=\tau(P_n),
 \qquad g(O;\eta_0)-\tau(P_n)=\phi_{P_n}(O)
\tag{8}
\]
by \(def:efficient\text{-}influence\text{-}function\).  For the nuisance
estimate trained outside fold \(s\), put
\(D_s(O)=g(O;\widehat\eta^{(-s)})-g(O;\eta_0)\).  Conditioning on the
training sample and evaluating (7) cell by cell gives the exact identity
\[
 P_nD_s=\sum_{k=1}^{d_n}p_k
 (\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}-\pi_k)
 \left\{
 \frac{\widehat\mu_{1k}^{(-s)}-\mu_{1k}}
      {\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}}
 +\frac{\widehat\mu_{0k}^{(-s)}-\mu_{0k}}
      {1-\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}}
 \right\}.
\tag{9}
\]
Every denominator in (9) is at least \(\epsilon/2\).  Cauchy--Schwarz and
(6) therefore show
\[
 |P_nD_s|=O_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(Md_n/n)
          =o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2}),
\tag{10}
\]
where the last step uses \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\) and the fixed scale \(M\).

The same score algebra, \(|\widehat\pi-\pi|\le1\), the clipped denominators,
and (2) imply
\[
 P_nD_s^2\le C_\epsilon\left[
 \sum_{a=0}^1\sum_{k=1}^{d_n}p_k
 (\widehat\mu_{ak}^{(-s)}-\mu_{ak})^2
 +M^2\sum_{k=1}^{d_n}p_k
 (\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}-\pi_k)^2\right]
 =O_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(M^2d_n/n).
\tag{11}
\]
By \(ass:iid\text{-}sampling\), the validation observations in \(I_s\) are
independent of \(\widehat\eta^{(-s)}\).  Conditional Chebyshev inequality and
(11) give
\[
 (\mathbb P_{I_s}-P_n)D_s
 =O_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(M\sqrt{d_n}/n).
\tag{12}
\]
Summing (9)--(12) over the fixed folds, with weights \(|I_s|/n\), and using
\(def:saturated\text{-}one\text{-}step\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)
 &=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{g(O_i;\eta_0)-\tau(P_n)\}
   +O_P(Md_n/n)+O_P(M\sqrt{d_n}/n)\\
 &=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{P_n}(O_i)
   +o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
\]

For the variance, \(ass:cell\text{-}mean\text{-}envelope\) and
\(def:ate\text{-}functional\) give \(|\tau(P_n)|\le2M\).
Using \(ass:fixed\text{-}overlap\),
\(ass:conditional\text{-}fourth\text{-}moment\), and
\(|x_1+x_2+x_3|^4\le27\sum_{j=1}^3|x_j|^4\) in
\(def:efficient\text{-}influence\text{-}function\) yields
\[
 E_{P_n}|\phi_{P_n}(O)|^4\le C_\epsilon M^4.
\tag{14}
\]
Consequently Chebyshev's inequality, (1), and (14) give
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{P_n}(O_i)^2
   -V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)=o_P(M^2),
 \qquad
 \overline\phi_n^2=o_P(M^2).
\tag{15}
\]
Conditioning fold by fold in (11) and applying Markov's inequality gives
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{s=0}^{K_0-1}\sum_{i\in I_s}D_s(O_i)^2
 =O_P(M^2d_n/n)=o_P(M^2).
\tag{16}
\]
For real arrays \((u_i)\) and \((v_i)\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \left|\frac1n\sum_i(u_i+v_i-\overline u-\overline v)^2
       -\frac1n\sum_i(u_i-\overline u)^2\right|
 \le2\left\{\frac1n\sum_i(u_i-\overline u)^2
             \frac1n\sum_i(v_i-\overline v)^2\right\}^{1/2}
      +\frac1n\sum_i(v_i-\overline v)^2.
\tag{17}
\]
Writing, for \(i\in I_s\),
\(\widehat\psi_i=\tau(P_n)+\phi_{P_n}(O_i)+D_s(O_i)\), and applying (17)
with \(u_i=\phi_{P_n}(O_i)\), \(v_i=D_s(O_i)\), equations (15)--(16) prove
\[
 \widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)=o_P(M^2).
\tag{18}
\]
Division is legitimate by the lower bound in (1), which proves
\(\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}/V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)\to1\).

Finally, (1) and (14) imply
\[
 \sup_n\frac{E_{P_n}|\phi_{P_n}(O)|^4}
                 {V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)^2}
 \le C_\epsilon/v_0^2<\infty.
\tag{19}
\]
The mean-zero identity needed by
\(lem:order\text{-}one\text{-}self\text{-}normalized\text{-}clt\) is (8);
\(ass:iid\text{-}sampling\) and (1) supply iid sampling and positive
variance.  That established lemma and (19) give
\[
 \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{P_n}(O_i)}
 {\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n[\phi_{P_n}(O_i)-\overline\phi_n]^2\right\}^{1/2}}
 \Rightarrow N(0,1).
\tag{20}
\]
Equation (15) makes the denominator in (20), divided by
\(\sqrt{nV_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)}\), converge in probability to one.  To avoid
invoking any undeclared limit theorem, fix \(x\in\mathbb R\) and
\(0<\delta<1\), and intersect with the event that this ratio lies in
\([1-\delta,1+\delta]\).  According to the sign of \(x\), the distribution
function of the oracle standardized mean is then bounded above and below by
the distribution functions in (20) evaluated at the smaller and larger of
\(x/(1-\delta)\) and \(x/(1+\delta)\), plus the probability of the complement
event.  First letting \(n\to\infty\), then \(\delta\downarrow0\), and using
continuity of the standard-normal distribution function gives
\[
 \frac{1}{\sqrt{nV_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)}}
 \sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{P_n}(O_i)\Rightarrow N(0,1).
\tag{21}
\]
Combining (13), (21), and the lower variance bound in (1) proves the asserted
normal limit.  This establishes every claim of the benchmark theorem without
using either heavy-light radius.
added_lemmas.justification: This theorem isolates the fully proved regular Gaussian benchmark without substituting it for the unresolved heavy-light theorem.
added_lemmas.gap: No estimator-side nuisance-rate assumption is imposed: the weighted cellwise rates and the orthogonal remainder are derived from the balanced masses, overlap, and fourth-moment envelope.

added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(m_0=|I_0|\).  The deterministic fold-size condition in
\(\mathcal I\) gives \(m_0\ge\lfloor n/K_0\rfloor\ge n/(2K_0)\) for all
sufficiently large \(n\).  For each \((a,k)\),
\(ass:iid\text{-}sampling\) makes
\(N_{ak}^{(0)}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(m_0,q_{ak})\), where
\[
 q_{ak}=P_n(X=k,A=a)\ge\epsilon p_k
 \ge\frac{\epsilon c_0}{d_n}.
\tag{1}
\]
The first inequality is \(ass:fixed\text{-}overlap\), and the second is
\(ass:balanced\text{-}cell\text{-}masses\).  Hence its mean
\(\lambda_{ak}=m_0q_{ak}\) obeys
\[
 \lambda_{ak}\ge\frac{\epsilon c_0n}{2K_0d_n}.
\tag{2}
\]
Assumption \(ass:local\text{-}dimension\) implies
\[
 \frac{n}{d_n\log(en)}
 =\frac{\sqrt n}{d_n}\frac{\sqrt n}{\log(en)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus (2) is at least \(512\log(en)\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).

For completeness, if \(Z\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(m,q)\) has mean
\(\lambda=mq\), exponential Markov inequality with \(t=\log2\), followed by
\(1+x\le e^x\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P\{Z\le\lambda/2\}
 &\le e^{t\lambda/2}E[e^{-tZ}]
 =e^{t\lambda/2}(1-q+qe^{-t})^m\\
 &\le\exp\{\lambda(t/2+e^{-t}-1)\}
 \le e^{-\lambda/8},
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
because \((\log2)/2-1/2<-1/8\).  Equations (2)--(4) therefore yield
\[
 Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\{N_{ak}^{(0)}\le256\log(en)\}
 \le\exp\!\left(-\frac{\epsilon c_0}{16K_0}\frac n{d_n}\right).
\tag{5}
\]
A union bound over the \(2d_n\) arm-cells, and the harmless enlargement
\(2d_n\le2d_nK_0\), prove the displayed bound.  Finally,
\(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\) implies
\(\log(2d_nK_0)-cn/d_n\to-\infty\), proving that its right-hand side is
\(o(1)\).
added_lemmas.justification: This is the probabilistic bridge that makes an exact all-heavy override useful on the balanced local class.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(d\le c_\epsilon n\log(en)\), the currently established
same-class confidence-length bounds are
\[
 r_{n,d,M}\lesssim_{\epsilon,\alpha}
 \mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}\le4M.
\]
The upper inequality is attained by the deterministic interval
\([-2M,2M]\); no direct calibration or Gaussian approximation is used.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The lower inequality is exactly
\(thm:same\text{-}class\text{-}testing\text{-}converse\), whose range
condition is the displayed restriction on \(d\).  For the upper inequality,
\(ass:cell\text{-}mean\text{-}envelope\) and
\(def:ate\text{-}functional\) imply
\[
 |\tau(P)|
 \le\sum_{k=1}^dp_k\{|\mu_{1k}|+|\mu_{0k}|\}
 \le2M
\]
for every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\).  Therefore the deterministic
interval \(C_n^0=[-2M,2M]\) has coverage one under every
\(Q_P^{(n)}\), is admissible in the infimum of
\(def:minimax\text{-}honest\text{-}length\), and has length \(4M\).
Taking the required supremum and infimum proves
\(\mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}\le4M\).
added_lemmas.justification: This records the strongest closed two-sided confidence-length statement presently justified by the core.
added_lemmas.gap: The upper endpoint \(4M\) is the deterministic range interval, so matching it to the lower scale remains the global calibration problem.
added_lemmas.consumer: It gives an honest fallback benchmark while the sharp constructive upper bound is unresolved.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 on pages 8--10 lower-bounds worst-case mean squared error for the one-arm functional \(\psi_1\) by the order of \(n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2 n]\) under fixed overlap; Appendix C.5 sets the control-arm regression to zero in the hard family.
The paper constructs heavy-light best-polynomial factorial-moment estimators attaining minimax mean squared error for additive discrete-distribution functionals.

Sections 4.1--4.2 provide scalar bounded-influence score inequalities, but they do not prove a tail theorem for this pilot-selected marked-factorial statistic; moreover, the symmetric half-log transform stipulated here is not globally monotone and needs a retained-range theorem or score replacement before root inversion is valid.
Theorem 1 lower-bounds expected confidence length in Gaussian nonparametric experiments by a between-class modulus and the paper constructs constant-factor adaptive intervals.
Theorem 5.1 gives uniformly valid asymptotically efficient Gaussian ATE intervals from cross-fitted orthogonal scores under nuisance-rate conditions.

The Abstract and Sections 2--4 derive finite-sample optimal bias-aware ATE estimators and confidence intervals under smoothness or shape restrictions when regression errors are normal with known variance, with feasible asymptotic extensions for unknown errors.

Theorem 3.1 gives a self-normalized moderate-deviation expansion for fixed-order nondegenerate Studentized U-statistics under moment conditions; its degree-one consequence is used only for the oracle-score central limit step.
The paper gives nearly tight dimension-free confidence intervals for probabilities of individually unobserved multinomial events.

open_obligations.what_is_open: An explicit data-measurable rare-cell score interval with a direct tail event, sharp expected radius, pilot-centering control, and certified root inversion for the selected marked-factorial statistic.
open_obligations.obstruction: The stipulated symmetric half-log score is redescending, has zero derivative at \(\pm\sqrt2\), and can have multiple roots. The core also lacks a score controlling the random shift between the pilot-conditional and unconditional centers.
open_obligations.attempted: The exact derivative and a one-remote-block configuration were analyzed before any moment-generating-function step; they disprove monotone unique-root inversion for the proposed score. The banked bias result does not supply the missing tail or pilot-shift certificate.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The established node \(lem:four\text{-}coordinate\text{-}bias\) supplies the
bias \(C_\epsilon Md/[n\log(en)]\).  The stipulated score does not yet turn
this fact into the requested observable tail radius.  Indeed, for
\[
 \psi(x)=\frac12\log\frac{1+x+x^2/2}{1-x+x^2/2}
\]
one has
\[
 \psi'(x)=\frac{2(2-x^2)}{x^4+4}.
\]
Thus the score is increasing only on \((-\sqrt2,\sqrt2)\) and is decreasing
outside that interval.  For any odd block count \(B\ge3\), any \(\lambda>0\),
and block outputs \(Z_1=\cdots=Z_{B-1}=0\), \(Z_B=R/\lambda\), the proposed
score is
\[
 S_R(t)=-(B-1)\psi(\lambda t)+\psi(R-\lambda t).
\]
For sufficiently large \(R\), continuity and
\(\psi(x)\downarrow0\) as \(x\to\infty\) give
\[
 S_R(0)>0,\quad S_R(\sqrt2/\lambda)<0,\quad
 S_R((R-\sqrt2)/\lambda)>0,\quad S_R(R/\lambda)<0.
\]
Hence the zero equation has at least three roots.  A retained-range argument
could repair uniqueness, but no such range, positive slope modulus, or
pilot-centering correction is currently defined.

proofs.proof_tex:
All unqualified expectations and probabilities below are taken under the
row law \(P_n\) and its i.i.d. sample law \(Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\), respectively.
Write
\[
 p_{k,n}=P_n(X=k),\qquad
 \pi_{k,n}=P_n(A=1\mid X=k),\qquad
 \sigma_{ak,n}^2
 =E_{P_n}\!\left[(Y-\mu_{ak,n})^2\mid X=k,A=a\right].
\]
The lower mass condition gives \(p_{k,n}\ge c_0/d>0\), and fixed overlap
then gives positive probability to both arm--cell events, so all displayed
conditional quantities are defined.  By the conditional fourth-moment
assumption and
\(\{E(Z^2)\}^2\le E(Z^4)\), which follows from
\(E[(Z^2-EZ^2)^2]\ge0\),
\[
 \sigma_{ak,n}^2\le M^2.                                             \tag{1}
\]
Put
\[
 h_{k,n}=\mu_{1k,n}-\mu_{0k,n}-\tau(P_n),\qquad
 V_n=V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n),\qquad \phi_n=\phi_{P_n}.
\]
The identifying equality in \(def:ate\text{-}functional\) gives
\(\sum_{k=1}^dp_{k,n}h_{k,n}=0\).  Conditional on \(X=k\), each outcome
residual in \(def:efficient\text{-}influence\text{-}function\) has mean zero,
and the treated and control residual terms have product zero because
\(A(1-A)=0\).  Expanding the square and then averaging over \(X\) therefore
gives
\[
 V_n=\sum_{k=1}^d p_{k,n}\left\{
 h_{k,n}^2+\frac{\sigma_{1k,n}^2}{\pi_{k,n}}
              +\frac{\sigma_{0k,n}^2}{1-\pi_{k,n}}
 \right\}.                                                           \tag{2}
\]
Every term in braces is nonnegative.  Since \(0<\pi_{k,n}<1\), for
\(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \sum_{k=1}^d p_{k,n}\sigma_{ak,n}^2\le V_n,
 \qquad
 \sum_{k=1}^d p_{k,n}h_{k,n}^2\le V_n.                               \tag{3}
\]

We first analyze the saturated one-step construction.  For validation fold
\(I_s\), define its training size \(m_{s,n}=n-|I_s|\) and the training
arm--cell count
\[
 \overline N_{ak}^{(-s)}
 =\sum_{j\notin I_s}\mathbf1\{X_j=k,A_j=a\}.
\]
Also set
\[
 q_{1k,n}=p_{k,n}\pi_{k,n},\qquad
 q_{0k,n}=p_{k,n}(1-\pi_{k,n}).
\]
The mass lower bound and fixed overlap imply
\[
 q_{ak,n}\ge q_*:=\frac{c_0\epsilon}{d}>0.                            \tag{4}
\]
Because \(K_0\) is fixed and the fold sizes differ by at most one, there is
a constant \(c_{mathrm{tr}}>0\), depending only on \(K_0\), such that
\(m_{s,n}\ge c_{mathrm{tr}}n\) for all folds and all sufficiently large
\(n\).  If \(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(m,q)\), then
\[
 P(N=0)=(1-q)^m\le e^{-mq}.                                           \tag{5}
\]
When \(mq\ge1\), splitting according to \(N\ge mq/2\) and applying
Markov's inequality to \((N-mq)^2\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}{N}\right]
 &\le \frac{2}{mq}+P(0<N<mq/2)\\
 &\le \frac{2}{mq}+\frac{4\operatorname{Var}(N)}{m^2q^2}
 \le\frac{6}{mq}.
 \end{aligned}                                                       \tag{6}
\]

Let
\[
 e_{ak}^{(-s)}=\widehat\mu_{ak}^{(-s)}-\mu_{ak,n},\qquad
 \delta_k^{(-s)}=\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}-\pi_{k,n}.
\]
Conditional on \(\overline N_{ak}^{(-s)}>0\), the outcome estimate in
\(def:saturated\text{-}one\text{-}step\) is a mean of that many independent
draws from the arm--cell law; it is unbiased and has conditional variance
\(\sigma_{ak,n}^2/\overline N_{ak}^{(-s)}\).  On the empty-cell event its
zero fallback has squared error at most \(M^2\) by the cell-mean envelope.
Equations \((4)\)--\((6)\) therefore imply, uniformly over the fixed set of
\((a,k,s)\),
\[
 E[(e_{ak}^{(-s)})^2]
 \le \frac{C\sigma_{ak,n}^2}{n}+CM^2e^{-cn}.                          \tag{7}
\]
For the propensity estimate, condition instead on the number of training
observations with \(X=k\).  On a nonempty cell the empirical treatment
fraction is unbiased with conditional variance at most the reciprocal of
that count; on an empty cell its squared error is at most one.  Clipping
cannot increase distance from
\(\pi_{k,n}\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\), because this interval is contained
in the clipping interval \([\epsilon/2,1-\epsilon/2]\).  Applying
\((5)\)--\((6)\) with \(p_{k,n}\ge c_0/d\) gives
\[
 E[(\delta_k^{(-s)})^2]\le \frac Cn+Ce^{-cn}.                         \tag{8}
\]
Here and below \(c,C>0\) may depend on
\((d,c_0,\epsilon,K_0)\), but not on \(n\) or on the row law.

Define the oracle uncentered score
\[
 \psi_n(O)=\mu_{1X,n}-\mu_{0X,n}
 +\frac{A(Y-\mu_{1X,n})}{\pi_{X,n}}
 -\frac{(1-A)(Y-\mu_{0X,n})}{1-\pi_{X,n}}
 =\tau(P_n)+\phi_n(O).                                                \tag{9}
\]
For \(i\in I_s\), put
\(D_{i,s}=\widehat\psi_i-\psi_n(O_i)\).  I.i.d. sampling and deterministic
sample splitting make \(O_i\) independent of the training sample
\(\mathcal D_n^{(-s)}=(O_j:j\notin I_s)\).  Direct substitution in the two
scores and conditional expectation over \(O_i\) give
\[
 E[D_{i,s}\mid X_i=k,\mathcal D_n^{(-s)}]
 =\delta_k^{(-s)}\left\{
 \frac{e_{1k}^{(-s)}}{\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}}
 +\frac{e_{0k}^{(-s)}}{1-\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}}
 \right\}.                                                          \tag{10}
\]
Both denominators are at least \(\epsilon/2\).  If
\(B_{s,n}=E[D_{i,s}\mid\mathcal D_n^{(-s)}]\), then Cauchy--Schwarz,
\((7)\), and \((8)\) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E|B_{s,n}|
 &\le \frac{2}{\epsilon}\sum_{a=0}^1\sum_{k=1}^d p_{k,n}
    \{E[(\delta_k^{(-s)})^2]E[(e_{ak}^{(-s)})^2]\}^{1/2}\\
 &\le \frac Cn\sum_{a=0}^1\sum_{k=1}^d p_{k,n}\sigma_{ak,n}
       +CMe^{-cn}\\
 &\le C\left\{\frac{\sqrt{V_n}}n+Me^{-cn}\right\}.
 \end{aligned}                                                       \tag{11}
\]
where the last line uses \(\sum_kp_{k,n}=1\), Cauchy--Schwarz, and
\((3)\).  The mean envelope and the identifying formula give
\(|h_{k,n}|\le4M\).  The inequality
\((x_1+x_2+x_3)^4\le27(x_1^4+x_2^4+x_3^4)\), the conditional
fourth-moment bound, and overlap then give
\[
 E_{P_n}[\phi_n(O)^4]\le C_\epsilon M^4,
 \qquad V_n\le C_\epsilon M^2.                                      \tag{12}
\]
Consequently \((11)\) and Markov's inequality show
\(\sqrt n B_{s,n}=o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(1)\), uniformly over the fixed number
of folds.

Before taking conditional expectation in \((10)\), the same score
substitution, the clipping bounds, and
\((x_1+\cdots+x_r)^2\le r\sum_jx_j^2\) give
\[
 E[D_{i,s}^2\mid\mathcal D_n^{(-s)}]
 \le C\sum_{k=1}^d p_{k,n}\left[
 (e_{1k}^{(-s)})^2+(e_{0k}^{(-s)})^2
 +(\delta_k^{(-s)})^2
       (\sigma_{1k,n}^2+\sigma_{0k,n}^2)
 \right].                                                           \tag{13}
\]
Taking expectations and applying \((3)\), \((7)\), and \((8)\) yields
\[
 E[D_{i,s}^2]\le \frac{CV_n}{n}+CM^2e^{-cn}=o(M^2).                  \tag{14}
\]
Conditional on \(\mathcal D_n^{(-s)}\), the centered variables
\(D_{i,s}-B_{s,n}\), \(i\in I_s\), are independent.  For each fold,
conditional variance and \((14)\) give
\[
 E\!\left[\left\{\frac1{\sqrt n}
   \sum_{i\in I_s}(D_{i,s}-B_{s,n})\right\}^2\right]
 \le \frac{|I_s|}{n}E[D_{i,s}^2]=o(M^2).
\]
Together with \(\sqrt nB_{s,n}=o_P(1)\) and fixed \(K_0\), the exact
decomposition
\[
 \frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{s=0}^{K_0-1}\sum_{i\in I_s}D_{i,s}
 =\sum_{s=0}^{K_0-1}\left\{
   \frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i\in I_s}(D_{i,s}-B_{s,n})
   +\frac{|I_s|}{\sqrt n}B_{s,n}\right\}
\]
therefore proves
\[
 \frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{s=0}^{K_0-1}\sum_{i\in I_s}D_{i,s}
 =o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(1).                                               \tag{15}
\]
Combining \((9)\), \((15)\), and the definition of
\(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}\) gives
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)\}
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_n(O_i)
  +o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(1).                                              \tag{16}
\]
The leading sum has mean zero and variance \(V_n\) by \((2)\).  Since the
premise \(V_n/M^2\to0\) and fixed \(M\) imply \(V_n\to0\), Markov's
inequality applied to its square and \((16)\) imply
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)\}
 \longrightarrow0                                                    \tag{17}
\]
in \(Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\)-probability.

For the variance estimator, independence and \((12)\) give
\[
 E\!\left[\left\{\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_n(O_i)^2-V_n\right\}^2\right]
 \le \frac{E[\phi_n(O)^4]}n
 \le \frac{C_\epsilon M^4}{n}.                                      \tag{18}
\]
Averaging \((14)\) over observations and applying Markov's inequality gives
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nD_{i,s(i)}^2=o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(M^2),             \tag{19}
\]
where \(s(i)\) is the fold containing \(i\).  Centering at the empirical
mean minimizes the empirical sum of squares, so
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 0\le\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}
 &\le\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat\psi_i-\tau(P_n)\}^2\\
 &\le\frac2n\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_n(O_i)^2
     +\frac2n\sum_{i=1}^nD_{i,s(i)}^2.
 \end{aligned}                                                       \tag{20}
\]
Equations \((18)\)--\((20)\) and \(V_n/M^2\to0\) prove
\[
 \widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}/M^2\longrightarrow0                       \tag{21}
\]
in probability.

It remains to transfer \((17)\) and \((21)\) to the corrected heavy--light
outputs.  Let
\[
 \mathcal H_n
 =\left\{\min_{a\in\{0,1\},\,1\le k\le d}N_{ak}^{(0)}
             >256\log(en)\right\}
 =\{\widehat{\mathcal L}=\varnothing\}.
\]
Because the pilot fold sizes differ from \(n/K_0\) by at most one, there is
\(c_{\mathrm{pil}}>0\), depending only on \(K_0\), such that
\(|I_0|\ge c_{\mathrm{pil}}n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Each
\(N_{ak}^{(0)}\) is binomial with mean
\(\nu_{ak,n}=|I_0|q_{ak,n}\ge c_{\mathrm{pil}}q_*n\), and hence
\(256\log(en)\le\nu_{ak,n}/2\) eventually.  For
\(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(m,q)\), exponential Markov with
\(t=\log2\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P(N\le mq/2)
 &\le e^{tmq/2}E[e^{-tN}]\\
 &=e^{tmq/2}(1-q+qe^{-t})^m\\
 &\le\exp\{mq[t/2-(1-e^{-t})]\}
 \le e^{-mq/8}.
 \end{aligned}                                                       \tag{22}
\]
because \(1-u\le e^{-u}\) and
\((1-\log2)/2>1/8\).  A union bound over the \(2d\) pilot arm--cells and
\((4)\) therefore gives
\[
 Q_{P_n}^{(n)}(\mathcal H_n^c)
 \le2d\exp\!\left(-\frac{c_{\mathrm{pil}}c_0\epsilon}{8d}n\right)
 \le2dK_0\exp\!\left(-\frac{c_{\mathrm{pil}}c_0\epsilon}{8d}n\right)
 =o(1).                                                              \tag{23}
\]
The corrected all-heavy clause of
\(def:robust\text{-}heavy\text{-}light\text{-}interval\text{-}handle\)
is the exact sample identity
\[
 (\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}},\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}})
 =(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}},\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}})
 \quad\text{on }\mathcal H_n.                                       \tag{24}
\]
Thus, for every \(r>0\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\!\left(\sqrt n
   |\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}-\tau(P_n)|>r\right)
 &\le Q_{P_n}^{(n)}(\mathcal H_n^c)
  +Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\!\left(\sqrt n
   |\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)|>r\right),\\
 Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\!\left(\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}}/M^2>r\right)
 &\le Q_{P_n}^{(n)}(\mathcal H_n^c)
  +Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\!\left(\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}/M^2>r\right).
 \end{aligned}                                                       \tag{25}
\]
Equations \((17)\), \((21)\), and \((23)\) prove both heavy--light
conclusions.  Notice that this transfer uses no asserted property of either
proposed confidence radius.

Finally, the non-implication is witnessed inside the same class.  Let
\(P_n=P^0\) for every \(n\), where \(X\) is uniform on
\(\{1,\ldots,d\}\), \(A\) is independent of \(X\) with
\(P^0(A=1)=1/2\), and \(Y(0)=Y(1)=Y=0\) almost surely.  Consistency and
conditional exchangeability hold by construction.  Fixed overlap holds
because \(\epsilon<1/2\); the cell-mean and conditional fourth-moment bounds
hold with value zero; and \(p_k=1/d\ge c_0/d\) because \(c_0\le1\).
The identifying functional and efficient-influence-function definition give
\(\tau(P^0)=0\) and \(\phi_{P^0}(O)=0\) almost surely, hence
\[
 V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^0)=0.                                           \tag{26}
\]
Consequently a statistic divided by
\(\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^0)}\), a variance ratio with denominator
\(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^0)\), and a Wald endpoint comparison normalized by
\(\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^0)/n}\) are undefined.  Since this sequence
satisfies every premise, those studentized or relative conclusions do not
follow on the stated class.  The witness makes no claim about an absolute
\(o_P(n^{-1/2})\) endpoint comparison.

Let \(\mathbf P=(P_n)\) satisfy \(P_n\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\),
\(d_n=d\) fixed, \(P_n(X=k)\ge c_0/d\) for every \(k\), and
\(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)/M^2\to0\).  Then
\(\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}-\tau(P_n)\}\to0\) and
\(\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)\}\to0\) in
\(Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\)-probability, while
\(\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}}/M^2\to0\) and
\(\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}/M^2\to0\).  No conclusion that requires division
by \(\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)}\) follows from these conditions alone; in
particular, they imply neither a standardized normal limit, nor ratio
consistency of either variance estimator, nor endpoint equivalence after
normalization by \(\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)/n}\).
